Question: How many whole numbers between \(1\) and \(1000\) do not contain the digit \(1?\)
Solution:
First count from \(0\) through \(999\), writing every number with exactly three digits by adding leading zeros when needed. For example, \(7\) becomes \(007\). Adding zeros does not introduce a digit \(1\), and every number has exactly one such representation.

Each position can contain any of the nine digits
\[
0,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9.
\]
Choosing the three positions gives
\[
9\cdot9\cdot9=729
\]
representations that avoid \(1\). This includes \(000\), which represents \(0\) and lies outside the requested range, so subtract one. The endpoints \(1\) and \(1000\) both contain \(1\) and contribute nothing.

The answer is
\[
729-1=\boxed{728},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
